task.situation: The online youth magazine ‘Crossroads’ is holding an essay competition. This year’s question is: ‘Is a young person an adult at 18?’ The best essays will be published on the magazine’s website. You decide to take part.
points: discuss the role of legal age limits, such as voting at 16 and coming of age at 18
explain which responsibilities young people take on as they grow up
evaluate how important independence from parents is for becoming an adult

words.long: Give your essay a title. Write around 400 words.

task.de: Essay für den Wettbewerb eines Online-Jugendmagazins: Ist man mit 18 erwachsen? Drei Inhaltspunkte: Altersgrenzen, Verantwortung, Unabhängigkeit von den Eltern. Zuerst wählt ihr eure Position, der Titel kommt ganz zum Schluss.

focus.label: linking words for an argument
focus.note: Marked: linking words that build an argument: concession and contrast (admittedly, whereas, nevertheless, even so), cause and result (since, therefore, as a result), examples, rephrasing and summary (for instance, in other words, to sum up). ‘And’, ‘but’, ‘because’, ‘also’ and time words such as ‘when’, ‘before’ or ‘until’ are not marked.

gaps.q: Which other responsibility do teenagers take on? Give a phrase that starts with a verb, e.g. ‘coach children at a football club’. Use ‘their’, not ‘my’.
gaps.qDe: Ruft eine weitere Pflicht von Jugendlichen als englische Wendung, die mit einem Verb beginnt, z. B. „coach children at a football club“ oder „pay their own phone bill“.
gaps.default: coach children at a football club

steps.q: ‘Is a young person an adult at 18?’ What is our position?
steps.de: Zuerst entscheidet ihr euch für eine Position, nach der sich das ganze Essay richtet.

options.label: Yes, at 18
options.teaser: At 18, the law treats young people as adults, and full rights and duties begin on the same day.

options.label: No, it is a process
options.teaser: A birthday does not make anyone an adult. Responsibility and independence matter far more than a date.

options.label: Partly
options.teaser: 18 is a sensible legal line, but real adulthood develops gradually over several years.

steps.q: How do we introduce the topic and state our thesis?
steps.de: Die Einleitung führt in die Frage des Essays ein. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction in your own words and end with a clear thesis statement.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Einleitung mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben. Am Ende steht eure These (Thesis Statement).

options.label: Start with a contrast
options.why: A short contrast and a question show that the issue is not simple; the thesis follows at the end.

map.yes: {{At first sight, the start of adulthood seems easy to date:}} in Austria, a person legally comes of age at 18. {{[[Admittedly,]] some teenagers are}} more mature than many adults. Should a single birthday really decide who counts as an adult? {{This essay will argue that}} 18 is the right place to draw the line, [[as]] full rights and real duties begin on that day.
map.no: {{At first sight, the start of adulthood seems easy to date:}} in Austria, a person legally comes of age at 18. {{[[In reality,]] some 17-year-olds}} already earn their own money, [[whereas]] some 25-year-olds still depend on their parents for almost everything. Can one birthday really turn a teenager into an adult overnight? {{This essay will argue that}} adulthood is a process rather than a date, shaped by responsibility and independence.
map.partly: {{At first sight, the start of adulthood seems easy to date:}} in Austria, a person legally comes of age at 18. {{[[In reality,]] maturity}} does not arrive overnight, and few people feel completely grown up on their 18th birthday. Does this make the legal age meaningless? {{This essay will argue that}} 18 is a sensible legal line, [[although]] real adulthood develops gradually as young people take on responsibility and become independent.

options.label: Name the issues
options.why: Names the three aspects of the task first, so the reader knows exactly what the essay will discuss.

map.yes: {{Adulthood can be discussed from several angles:}} it may be seen as a legal status, a set of duties or the freedom to run one’s own life. {{Some people believe that}} these develop separately, [[as]] many teenagers earn their own money long before they may sign a contract alone. {{This essay will argue that}} all three come together at 18, [[which is why]] this birthday marks the true start of adulthood.
map.no: {{Adulthood can be discussed from several angles:}} it may be seen as a legal status, a set of duties or the freedom to run one’s own life. {{Only the first of these}} is linked to a fixed age. {{This essay will argue that}} the legal status matters least, [[whereas]] responsibility and independence are what really turn a young person into an adult.
map.partly: {{Adulthood can be discussed from several angles:}} it may be seen as a legal status, a set of duties or the freedom to run one’s own life. {{These three, [[however,]] rarely arrive together.}} {{This essay will argue that}} the legal status sensibly begins at 18, [[whereas]] the other two develop gradually over several years and differ from one young person to the next.

options.label: Start with the law
options.text: In Austria, young people may vote at 16, but they cannot sign a contract alone until they are 18. Many teenagers find these rules confusing, and even their parents are often not sure what is allowed at which age. This essay will therefore explain the most important age limits in Austrian law and describe what young people are allowed to do at 15, 16 and 18.
options.reject: Off target: the question is whether a young person is an adult at 18, but this thesis only promises a description of age limits. The introduction must end with a thesis that answers the question.
options.rejectDe: Am Thema vorbei: Gefragt ist, ob man mit 18 erwachsen ist, doch diese These kündigt nur eine Beschreibung der Altersgrenzen an. Die Einleitung endet mit einer These, die die Frage beantwortet.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1: what role do legal age limits play, and what example shows it?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: Altersgrenzen, mit einem Beispiel. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then support the topic sentence with facts about age limits (the teacher writes them on the board) and say what they show about adulthood.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Topic Sentence mit Fakten zu Altersgrenzen stützen (sie stehen an der Tafel) und sagen, was sie über das Erwachsensein zeigen.

options.label: Why age limits exist
options.why: The topic sentence explains why age limits exist; the voting age at 16 then tests the point.

map.yes: {{The legal side of adulthood is the easiest to define: every society needs clear rules.}} {{[[Since]]}} the maturity of each teenager cannot be tested individually, one date has to be fixed. At 18, young Austrians may sign contracts alone and even stand for parliament. {{It is true that in 2007 Austria became}} the first EU country to lower the voting age to 16. {{Voting, [[however,]] carries no personal risk,}} {{[[whereas]]}} a contract signed at 18 can bring debts that last for years. {{[[In short,]] only at 18}} does the law trust young people with decisions of this weight.
map.no: {{The legal side of adulthood is the easiest to define: every society needs clear rules.}} {{[[Since]]}} the maturity of each teenager cannot be tested individually, one date has to be fixed. {{[[However,]] a date chosen for practical reasons}} says little about actual maturity. {{The voting age is a good example. When Austria became}} the first EU country to lower it to 16 in 2007, critics feared that teenagers would not take this right seriously. {{[[In fact,]]}} research suggests that most 16-year-olds vote as carefully as older voters. {{This shows that}} maturity can be present long before the 18th birthday.
map.partly: {{The legal side of adulthood is the easiest to define: every society needs clear rules.}} {{[[Since]]}} the maturity of each teenager cannot be tested individually, one date has to be fixed, and 18 makes good sense. {{[[Nevertheless,]]}} such a line is a practical tool and cannot measure maturity precisely. {{The voting age shows this well. When Austria became}} the first EU country to lower it to 16 in 2007, critics feared that teenagers would not take this right seriously. {{The experience has been largely positive.}} {{[[Even so,]]}} voting is only one part of being an adult.

options.label: Rights at 15, 16 and 18

map.yes: If you’re a young Austrian, you get your rights step by step. At 15, you’re allowed to start an apprenticeship, and at 16 you can vote in every election. You can’t sign a contract on your own, though, until you’re 18. That isn’t the same everywhere: Austria only lowered the age from 19 to 18 in 2001, and Japan didn’t change it from 20 to 18 until 2022. Since most countries have chosen 18, it’s clear that this is the birthday when you’re finally trusted with your own life, and that’s why the line makes sense.
map.no: If you’re a young Austrian, you get your rights step by step. At 15, you’re allowed to start an apprenticeship, and at 16 you can vote in every election. You can’t sign a contract on your own, though, until you’re 18. That isn’t the same everywhere: Austria only lowered the age from 19 to 18 in 2001, and Japan didn’t change it from 20 to 18 until 2022. If a line can be moved like that, it doesn’t tell you much about how mature you really are. You don’t suddenly become an adult on your birthday just because the law says so.
map.partly: If you’re a young Austrian, you get your rights step by step. At 15, you’re allowed to start an apprenticeship, and at 16 you can vote in every election. You can’t sign a contract on your own, though, until you’re 18. That isn’t the same everywhere: Austria only lowered the age from 19 to 18 in 2001, and Japan didn’t change it from 20 to 18 until 2022. So the line’s a political choice, but it’s still useful because you know what’s expected of you. You don’t become fully mature overnight, and nobody expects you to.

options.reject: Wrong register for an essay: it talks to the reader as ‘you’ and is full of contractions (you’re, can’t, isn’t, didn’t). An essay is formal and impersonal: ‘young people’, ‘cannot’, ‘is not’.
options.rejectDe: Falsches Register für ein Essay: Der Absatz spricht die Leser:innen mit „you“ an und steckt voller Kurzformen (you’re, can’t, isn’t, didn’t). Ein Essay ist formell und unpersönlich.

options.label: Rights step by step
options.why: ‘Legally’ links to the introduction; Austrian age limits and a look abroad support the point.

map.yes: {{Legally, young Austrians gain their rights step by step.}} At 15, they may start an apprenticeship, and at 16 they are allowed to vote. {{[[Yet]] only at 18 do they gain}} full legal capacity, which allows them to sign contracts alone. {{History and other countries show that}} this line is not fixed by nature: Austria lowered it from 19 to 18 in 2001, and Japan from 20 to 18 in 2022. {{[[Nevertheless,]] the fact that}} most countries have settled on 18 shows broad agreement that this is the age at which people are ready to take charge of their lives.
map.no: {{Legally, young Austrians gain their rights step by step.}} At 15, they may start an apprenticeship, at 16 they may vote, and at 18 they can sign contracts alone. {{[[In other words,]] even the law does not see}} adulthood as a single moment. {{History and other countries show that}} the line is a political decision: Austria lowered it from 19 to 18 in 2001, and Japan from 20 to 18 in 2022. {{A line that moves so easily}} can hardly mark a natural turning point. {{[[Instead,]]}} it says more about a country’s history than about its young people.
map.partly: {{Legally, young Austrians gain their rights step by step.}} At 15, they may start an apprenticeship, at 16 they may vote, and at 18 they can sign contracts alone. {{Such a gradual approach is sensible:}} it lets teenagers grow into their rights. {{History and other countries show that}} the exact age is a political choice: Austria lowered it from 19 to 18 in 2001, and Japan from 20 to 18 in 2022. {{[[Even so,]] a fixed age is useful, [[as]]}} a clear line protects young people and tells them what is expected of them.

steps.q: Body paragraph 2: which responsibilities do young people take on?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: Verantwortung, die junge Menschen übernehmen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then give two examples of responsibilities that teenagers take on (not the ones from the board) and explain what they show.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann zwei Beispiele für Pflichten von Jugendlichen nennen (nicht die vom Beamer) und erklären, was sie zeigen.

options.label: Busy teenage lives
options.text: Secondly, many teenagers have a part-time job, help at home or look after younger brothers and sisters. Some of them also have to make big decisions about school and their future career at a young age. Apprentices start work at 15 and often get up very early, while pupils at academic schools have lessons until the afternoon and homework in the evening. Many teenagers also do sport, play an instrument or help in a club at the weekend. This is not always easy, and they need a lot of time and energy for it, especially during the busy school year.
options.reject: There is no topic sentence: the paragraph starts with examples and lists one activity after another, so the reader never learns its main idea. And ‘Secondly’ needs a ‘First’ before it, which our essay does not have.
options.rejectDe: Kein Topic Sentence: Der Absatz beginnt gleich mit Beispielen und zählt nur Tätigkeiten auf. Und „Secondly“ ohne vorheriges „First“ passt nicht.

options.label: Everyday duties
options.why: ‘Apart from rights’ links back to the legal side; everyday examples follow, and the class adds one of its own.

map.yes: {{Apart from rights, growing up brings a range of new responsibilities.}} Many teenagers take on summer jobs, look after younger siblings or {DUTY}. {{In most families, [[though,]] these duties are shared}} with parents, who step in when something goes wrong. A forgotten shift or a missed appointment rarely has lasting effects for a 16-year-old. {{This changes on the 18th birthday.}} From that day on, young people are responsible for their own contracts, debts and mistakes. {{It is [[therefore]] this moment}} that turns years of practice into real responsibility.
map.no: {{Apart from rights, growing up brings a range of new responsibilities,}} many of them long before 18. Sixteen-year-old apprentices work full days, and many pupils look after younger siblings or {DUTY}. {{Taking on such duties}} teaches reliability and good planning because other people depend on the result: a family that counts on a teenager to collect a child from school cannot afford a forgotten afternoon. {{[[By contrast,]]}} a 20-year-old who has never had to care for anyone may still lack this experience. {{[[Therefore,]] responsibility, not age,}} is the better measure of adulthood.
map.partly: {{Apart from rights, growing up brings a range of new responsibilities,}} which increase during the teenage years. A 14-year-old may look after a younger sibling, [[whereas]] a 17-year-old might have a summer job and {DUTY}. {{Each new duty brings}} a little more trust from parents and a little less control. Mistakes made at this stage usually have limited effects: {{[[after all,]]}} an adult is still there to help. {{By the age of 18, most young people}} have had years of practice before the law makes them fully responsible for their actions.

options.label: Decisions about the future
options.why: The topic sentence turns from rights to responsibility; school and career choices are typical for Austrian teenagers.

map.yes: {{Rights are only one side of adulthood: responsibility for one’s own future is just as central.}} Austrian teenagers make important choices early, [[such as]] whether to stay at school after the age of 15 or to begin an apprenticeship. {{These choices, [[though,]] are made}} with their parents’ support, and a parent signs every important form. {{At 18, support turns into advice:}} young people may still ask their families, but they decide and sign alone. If a decision proves wrong, they have to live with the results. {{[[For this reason,]]}} the 18th birthday is the real test of responsibility.
map.no: {{Rights are only one side of adulthood: responsibility for one’s own future is just as central,}} and Austrian teenagers take it on remarkably early. At around 14, they choose between an academic school, a vocational college and an apprenticeship. {{Choices like these shape a whole life,}} {{[[yet]]}} they are made years before the law calls anyone an adult. A teenager who starts an apprenticeship at 15 signs a training contract and has to be at work on time every day. {{Such a decision [[therefore]] requires}} the same planning for the future that is expected of adults.
map.partly: {{Rights are only one side of adulthood: responsibility for one’s own future is just as central and grows with age.}} At around 14, Austrian teenagers choose their next school with their parents’ help, [[whereas]] at 17 many plan their studies or career on their own. {{The decisions become bigger}} as the support becomes smaller. A school leaver must decide where to study, how to pay for it and whether to move to another city. {{[[As a result,]] the legal step at 18}} is the natural end of a slow development rather than a sudden change.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3: how important is independence from parents, and what does the other side say?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: Unabhängigkeit von den Eltern, mit einem Gegenargument. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then evaluate independence in your own words and answer the counter-argument.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Unabhängigkeit mit eigenen Worten bewerten und das Gegenargument entkräften.

options.label: Money and a home of one’s own
options.why: ‘Beyond responsibility’ links back; the paragraph weighs the common view and answers a counter-argument.

map.yes: {{Beyond responsibility, financial independence is often seen as the clearest sign of adulthood.}} Many young Austrians live with their parents until their mid-twenties, [[for example]] while studying. {{It could be argued that}} they are not yet adults, [[as]] they still depend on their families for housing and food. {{[[Even so,]] financial support is not the same as parental control.}} Once they turn 18, young people are free to decide where to live, what to study and how to spend their money. {{[[In other words,]] living at home is}} often a practical choice rather than a sign of childhood.
map.no: {{Beyond responsibility, financial independence is often seen as the clearest sign of adulthood.}} Many young Austrians live with their parents until their mid-twenties, [[for example]] while they are at university. {{[[Although]] they are legally adults,}} they rely on their families for housing and food. {{It could be argued that}} turning 18 still brings independence: banks, landlords and employers suddenly deal with young people directly. {{This is true in legal terms.}} {{Being treated as an adult, [[though,]]}} is not the same as being one, and many only feel grown up once they can pay their own way.
map.partly: {{Beyond responsibility, financial independence is often seen as the clearest sign of adulthood,}} {{[[yet]]}} it rarely arrives at 18. Many young Austrians live with their parents until their mid-twenties, [[for example]] while studying. {{It could be argued that}} independence is either there or not, and that a gradual view simply avoids a clear answer. {{[[In fact,]] independence has several sides:}} a young person may manage their own money long before they can run a household or deal with officials alone. {{Each of these skills develops at its own speed,}} and no single date can capture them all.

options.label: Standing on one’s own feet
options.why: Links responsibility and independence, looks beyond money and then answers the other side.

map.yes: {{Responsibility goes hand in hand with independence, a matter of attitude as much as of money.}} Adults solve their own problems and accept the results of their decisions. {{Critics of a fixed age point out that}} such independence comes from experience, not from a birthday: an 18-year-old who has never paid a bill or dealt with an official is hardly independent. {{[[Still,]] these skills are learnt quickly}} once young people are allowed to make their own decisions. {{[[This is why]] the legal age matters so much:}} at 18, the law finally gives them exactly this chance.
map.no: {{Responsibility goes hand in hand with independence, a matter of attitude as much as of money.}} Adults solve their own problems and accept the results of their decisions. {{Many teenagers show this kind of maturity}} long before they come of age, [[for instance]] when they settle a conflict alone. {{Opponents of this view point out that}} at 18 young people may leave home or open a bank account without permission. {{Such freedom, [[though,]] is only an opportunity:}} a young person who still needs help with every decision has gained a right, but not yet the ability to use it.
map.partly: {{Responsibility goes hand in hand with independence, a matter of attitude as much as of money.}} Adults solve their own problems and accept the results of their decisions. {{Independence from parents develops slowly,}} {{[[since]]}} it is learnt through years of experience, and the law merely marks the point where this learning should be well advanced. {{Opponents of a balanced view would argue that}} young people need one clear message about when they must stand on their own feet. {{[[Still,]] young people are perfectly able}} to understand that legal and personal independence are two different things.

options.label: Living at home

map.yes: Independence from parents is also very important for becoming an adult. Many young people live by their parents until they are 25 because the money from their job is too less. A flat in the city is expensive, and they also have to pay for food, electricity and clothes. Only when they move out, they notice how much an adult life really costs. However, at 18 they are legally free to make this decision, and most of them learn to manage their money quickly once they have to. This is why 18 is a sensible age for adulthood.
map.no: Independence from parents is also very important for becoming an adult. Many young people live by their parents until they are 25 because the money from their job is too less. A flat in the city is expensive, and they also have to pay for food, electricity and clothes. Only when they have their own flat and pay their own bills, they are real adults. Turning 18 does not change this situation, as a birthday does not pay the rent. Real independence comes slowly, through work and experience.
map.partly: Independence from parents is also very important for becoming an adult. Many young people live by their parents until they are 25 because the money from their job is too less. A flat in the city is expensive, and they also have to pay for food, electricity and clothes. Only when they can pay all their own bills, they are fully independent. At 18 they gain the legal right to decide for themselves, but financial independence often takes several more years. Both steps are part of growing up.

options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘live by their parents’ (→ live with), ‘too less’ (→ too little) and ‘Only when …, they’ (→ Only when … do they / are they: inversion, no comma).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: live by → live with, too less → too little, und nach „Only when …“ folgt die Inversion (do they / are they), ohne Beistrich.

steps.q: Conclusion: how do we end the essay?
steps.de: Der Schluss rundet das Essay ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then sum up our position and the main points of the three body paragraphs in two or three sentences of your own.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann unsere Position und die Hauptpunkte der drei Body Paragraphs in zwei bis drei eigenen Sätzen zusammenfassen.

options.label: Sum up the position
options.why: ‘To sum up’ and an impersonal phrase restate the thesis and pick up all three points without ‘I think’.

map.yes: {{[[To sum up,]] it seems clear that}} 18 is the age at which a young person becomes an adult. The law needs one fixed date, and this one is well chosen. {{[[Even though]]}} teenagers take on duties early and many stay at home longer, only this birthday brings full rights, full responsibility and the freedom to decide alone. {{It is the day on which}} childhood ends in legal terms.
map.no: {{[[To sum up,]] it seems clear that}} adulthood cannot be reduced to a single date. The law needs a fixed age to work, and 18 is as good as any other. {{Real adulthood, [[on the other hand,]]}} grows out of the duties young people accept and the independence they gain over time. {{For some, this happens at 16,}} for others not until their late twenties.
map.partly: {{[[To sum up,]] it seems clear that}} the law needs a fixed age, and 18 is a reasonable choice. {{[[At the same time,]]}} it marks just one milestone in a long process: young people take on duties years before this birthday and often become independent of their parents years after it. {{Adulthood is [[thus]] best understood}} as a gradual development with a clear legal line somewhere in the middle.

options.label: Look back on the essay
options.why: Looks back on rights, duties and independence and ends with a clear final statement.

map.yes: {{[[In conclusion,]] this essay has shown that}} the 18th birthday is more than a symbolic date. Teenagers practise responsibility for years, and many still live at home long after 18. {{The decisive change, [[however,]]}} comes when the law grants them full rights together with full responsibility. {{From this day on,}} they are free to run their own lives, which makes 18 the real beginning of adult life.
map.no: {{[[In conclusion,]] this essay has shown that}} the 18th birthday is mainly a legal milestone. Teenagers often take on serious duties years earlier, [[whereas]] many legal adults still rely on their families. {{Young people become adults when}} they are ready to stand on their own feet, and this happens at a different age for everyone. {{A birthday can mark this moment,}} but it cannot create it.
map.partly: {{[[In conclusion,]] this essay has shown that}} the 18th birthday is an important legal milestone, but not the whole story. Duties increase gradually during adolescence, and independence from parents often takes much longer. {{Becoming an adult is [[therefore]]}} a gradual process, and the law simply draws its line at a sensible point along the way.

options.label: Add one more point
options.text: In conclusion, the question is more difficult than it seems, and there are good arguments on both sides. A further point is that young people today grow up faster than their grandparents did, as they have access to the internet and social media from an early age. They see much more of the adult world than earlier generations. Schools should therefore teach adult skills such as taxes and contracts much earlier.
options.reject: A conclusion sums up the position on the basis of the arguments already given. This one brings in a new argument (the internet) and a new demand, and our position disappears.
options.rejectDe: Im Schluss kommen keine neuen Argumente oder Forderungen. Hier taucht plötzlich das Internet auf, und unsere Position verschwindet.

steps.q: Now that the essay is finished, which title do we choose?
steps.de: Zuletzt wählen wir den Titel für unser Essay.
steps.own: Factual and to the point: the title names the topic and fits our position.
steps.ownDe: Sachlich: Der Titel nennt das Thema und passt zu unserer Position.

options.label: State the position
options.why: A short statement title tells the reader the topic and the position at once.

map.yes: Eighteen: the age at which adulthood begins
map.no: Adulthood: a process, not a date
map.partly: Adulthood: a legal line and a gradual process

options.label: Explain the position
options.why: Factual and clear, and it already hints at the argument of the essay.

map.no: Why adulthood cannot be measured in years
map.partly: Coming of age: legal status and personal maturity

options.label: Name the topic
options.why: Neutral and factual: it names the topic without giving away the answer.

checks.en: A factual title that states the topic (a statement, not a question)
The introduction ends with a thesis statement that shows our position
All three content points: legal age limits, responsibilities, independence
Every body paragraph starts with a topic sentence
Each body paragraph links back to what came before
Formal register: no contractions, no ‘you’, no personal stories
The conclusion sums up our position without new arguments

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam ein Essay nach SRDP-Standard auf B1+/B2-Niveau: sachlicher Titel, Einleitung mit Thesis Statement, drei Body Paragraphs mit Topic Sentences, Schluss ohne neue Argumente. Fokus: Linking words für Argumentation und Gegensatz über and, but und because hinaus.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen (ohne Karten: 1–4 Finger, die Tasten 1–4 wählen wie A–D), Beamer im Vollbild. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min für Einleitung und Schluss, 8 min pro Body Paragraph.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum (rechts), „Essay“ als Überschrift, darunter 2 Zeilen für den Titel frei lassen (der Titel kommt zuletzt). Jeder Absatz beginnt nach einer Leerzeile, am Rand stehen Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3, Conclusion. Linking words grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: Volltext (Doppelstunde, 100 min): 5 min Aufgabe lesen und Position wählen, dann 6 Entscheidungen (fünf Absätze, zuletzt der Titel) à ca. 2–3 min, Abschreiben ca. 45 min, 5 min Checkliste. Gerüst (Doppelstunde, 100 min): 3 min Aufgabe und Position; pro Absatz 2 min Abstimmung, dann eigenes Schreiben (Einleitung und Schluss je 5 min, Body Paragraphs je 8 min) und 2 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; am Ende 3 min Titel und 5 min Checkliste. Wird die Zeit knapp, Schluss und Titel als Hausübung. Bei Body 1 nach der Abstimmung die Fakten der gewählten Option kurz an die Tafel schreiben (z. B. 15/16/18, 2007/EU bzw. 2001/2022), weil die Optionen danach verschwinden.
teacher.traps: Introduction C (TA): Die These beantwortet die Frage nicht, sie kündigt nur eine Beschreibung der Altersgrenzen an. Body 1 B (LSR): Plauderton mit „you“ und vielen Kurzformen (you’re, can’t, isn’t, didn’t) statt formeller, unpersönlicher Sprache. Body 2 A (CC): kein Topic Sentence, nur eine Aufzählung von Tätigkeiten, dazu „Secondly“ ohne „First“. Body 3 C (LSA): live by statt live with, too less statt too little, fehlende Inversion nach „Only when …“. Conclusion C (TA): Die Position verschwindet (darum TA), dazu kommen ein neues Argument und eine neue Forderung. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Das Essay hat fünf Absätze (Einleitung, drei Body Paragraphs mit je einem Inhaltspunkt, Schluss) und wie bei der SRDP eine Länge: ca. 400 Wörter. Jede Entscheidung ist ein ganzer Absatz; Body 3 nimmt in jeder Option ein Gegenargument auf und entkräftet es. Keine persönlichen Erfahrungen mit Konflikten im Elternhaus einfordern. Die erste Entscheidung (Position yes / no / partly) bestimmt Thesis, Topic Sentences und Schluss in allen Absätzen: Gut eignet sich eine kurze Abstimmung mit Begründung. Fakten im Text: Wählen ab 16 (seit 2007, erstes EU-Land), Volljährigkeit ab 18 (seit 2001, davor 19), Japan 2022 von 20 auf 18. Wählt die Klasse in Body 2 Option B, ruft sie eine weitere Pflicht von Jugendlichen als englische Wendung mit Verb am Anfang und mit „their“ (z. B. „pay their own phone bill“). Mit der Taste P werden Linking words grün markiert, hier vor allem solche für Argumentation und Gegensatz (Einräumen, Gegensatz, Grund und Folge); „since“ ist nur dort markiert, wo es „weil“ bedeutet, nicht „seit“. Differenzierung: Schnelle schreiben im Gerüst-Modus einen zusätzlichen Beispielsatz pro Absatz. Hausübung: zweite Fassung mit einer anderen Position.
